name: Boat Pose
intro:
Boat Pose (Navasana) is a powerful core-strengthening yoga posture that helps build stability, balance, and endurance. In this pose, the body forms a V-shape by balancing on the sitting bones while lifting the legs and extending the arms forward. This position actively engages the abdominal muscles, hip flexors, and spine, making it an effective pose for strengthening the core.

Navasana not only improves physical strength but also enhances focus and mental determination. Holding the pose requires concentration and controlled breathing, which helps develop mind-body awareness. It is often included in yoga routines aimed at improving balance, posture, and overall body control.

Regular practice of Boat Pose helps tone the abdominal muscles, improve digestion, and increase stamina. It is especially beneficial for people looking to strengthen their core and reduce belly fat. Despite its intensity, practicing with proper alignment and breath control can make it accessible and highly rewarding for both beginners and experienced practitioners.

steps.text: Sit on the mat with your legs extended straight in front of you.
Lean back slightly while keeping your spine straight.
Lift your legs off the ground, balancing on your sitting bones.
Extend your arms forward parallel to the ground.
Hold the position while breathing steadily.

avoid: You have severe back pain or spinal injuries
You have hernia or recent abdominal surgery
You feel dizziness while performing the pose
You have heart conditions (consult a doctor)
You experience discomfort or strain in the lower back
